pending_commit.commit_message: vm_tools: concierge: Run crosvm commands synchronously Currently concierge spawns a process to run a crosvm command but doesn't wait for it to exit. This is a problem at suspend time because concierge will report suspend readiness to powerd and the crosvm command process will race with the system going to suspend. If the system suspends before all vcpus have been stopped the guest kernel will panic on resume because it thinks there is a soft lockup. Always wait for the crosvm command process to complete before continuing. BUG=chromium:946847 TEST=suspend and resume a device with a VM running. check the logs to see that the "Setting resolv config" message appears in the logs after crosvm logs that the run mode has changed to running. Change-Id: Iba91729e126319c59f030d932003ffff3bd8e549 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1541848 Commit-Ready: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

vm_tools: concierge: Properly clean up child exits If crosvm exits on its own (for example, due to a guest kernel panic) then concierge doesn't delete the TerminaVm pointer correspending to that VM from the `termina_vms_` field in the Service class. This is a problem because the pointer is now pointing to freed memory and will cause a segfault if we try to dereference it later. Make sure to delete the TerminaVm pointer and also notify cicerone that the VM was stopped. BUG=chromium:946852 TEST=stop a running vm with maitred_client, run `concierge_client --sync_times`, and observe that concierge does not crash Change-Id: I75f67f1e689a63d0be074962bb986b5ae688140d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1541849 Commit-Ready: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

sepolicy: attribute and categorize every Chrome OS file type. Introduce the new attributes for Chrome OS files: - cros_file_type: all file_type that's owned by Chrome OS, including user downloads. - cros_system_file_type: all cros_file_type that's distributed with the system image. - cros_var_file_type: all cros_file_type under /var but not /run (a.k.a /var/run) or /var/empty - cros_run_file_type: all cros_file_type under /run - cros_uncategorized_file_type: all other cros_file_type files And atribute all Chrome OS owned fs_type to any of them above. Add i2c-pseudo Linux kernel module. This Linux kernel module provides I2C adapters that can be backed by userspace programs. This allows for userspace implementations of functionality such as tunneling I2C through another communication channel to a remote I2C bus. BRANCH=none BUG=b:79684405 TEST=Used i2c-tools CLI to i2c-dev to issue I2C queries, and Python interactive interpreter as the I2C pseudo adapter controller. The i2c-pseudo module correctly proxied write, read, write+read, and multi-byte reads through the controller character device, and it correctly proxied back the responses from the character device, including the specific byte values read. Later, I implemented an I2C pseudo controller in Servod and used it to flash an ITE EC over I2C using both Servo Micro and Suzy-Q. Change-Id: Idda764e56b9e9d577302b59286e873291ea36d25 Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1250029 Reviewed-by: Nick Sanders <nsanders@chromium.org>
